title: Learning in the Right Subspace: Personalized Differential Private Federated Learning with Noise Filtering

problem.claim: Federated learning uses differential privacy to enhance model security, but heterogeneous user privacy preferences create personalized privacy requirements.

gap.claim: Uniform privacy budgets can waste privacy budgets for some clients and reduce overall model utility because they must comply with the most stringent budget.

contributions.claim: FedSPA is a personalized differential private federated learning framework based on subspace projection aggregation.

FedSPA applies singular value decomposition to noise-perturbed local models, clusters clients, identifies a consensus subspace, projects models with varying noise levels, and aggregates through a residual-aware mechanism.
The framework is designed to guide aggregation of client-personalized differential privacy while reducing communication overhead.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments demonstrate the model's effectiveness.
The authors report providing theoretical proofs of FedSPA's privacy and convergence.
The authors report superior performance over personalized differential privacy federated learning baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Differential privacy is widely used in federated learning for model security.
Uniform privacy budgets overlook heterogeneous privacy preferences and can waste budgets while harming utility.
FedSPA represents noise-perturbed local models with singular value vectors, clusters clients, finds a consensus subspace, and performs residual-aware aggregation.
The method is reported to support personalized privacy aggregation and reduce communication overhead.
Experiments and theoretical analysis are reported to support effectiveness, privacy, convergence, and performance over personalized DP-FL baselines.

source_observation.claim: Uniform privacy configurations must satisfy the most stringent client budget, potentially wasting other clients' privacy budgets and reducing utility.

interpretation.claim: Privacy allocation in federated learning may need to account for client heterogeneity rather than applying one global budget.

application.claim: Systems with heterogeneous privacy preferences could consider client-specific privacy policies and aggregation mechanisms.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when personalized budgets outperform uniform budgets or how the approach behaves under different privacy distributions.

source_observation.claim: The method uses singular-value representations and consensus-subspace projection to handle models with varying noise levels.

interpretation.claim: Subspace-based representations may help separate shared model structure from privacy noise during aggregation.

application.claim: Related distributed learning systems could investigate structure-aware aggregation for heterogeneous model perturbations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the conditions under which the extracted subspace remains reliable or the communication reduction achieved.

unknowns: The abstract does not report dataset names, model architectures, privacy-budget ranges, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the privacy and convergence assumptions or proof conditions.
The abstract does not specify the amount of communication overhead reduction.
